speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you describe the appearance of the rash on your scalp and forehead, and tell me when it first started?

speaker: Patient
text: 3-month-old boy. The parents report that the rash has been present for several weeks, noting that it sometimes appears red and scaly, especially during cold weather. The patient was born at 36 weeks' gestation and has been generally healthy since. The patient's father has a history of psoriasis.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the rash cause itching, and do you notice any crusting or "cradle cap" appearance on the scalp? Are there similar rashes in the diaper area or skin folds?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Rash on scalp and forehead. I also have Erythematous patches, Greasy yellow scales, Worse in cold weather.

speaker: Doctor
text: Are there any similar greasy scales or red patches in the diaper area or skin folds, and does the baby seem itchy or irritable? I would also like to rule out other causes, so I will request a visual exam of the skin. REQUEST IMAGES

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Premature birth (36 weeks), otherwise generally healthy. Family history of psoriasis. Social history: The patient is 3 months old, so the social history is not applicable.

speaker: Doctor
text: The images confirm erythematous patches with greasy yellow scales on the scalp and forehead. This clinical presentation is classic for infantile seborrheic dermatitis, often called "cradle cap." DIAGNOSIS READY: Infantile Seborrheic Dermatitis
